The published excerpt 'oppose new local data centers.' cuts out the subject and the party percentages, which are the words that actually support the claim, so readers see a meaningless fragment. Restore the full sentence. The explanation also says the release warns that subgroup uncertainty exceeds the full-sample margin of error. That warning isn't in the frozen context, so it can't be confirmed.

Rationale matches e1: 48.9% to 60.6%, +11.8 points, 95% CI +6.9 to +16.6, within-person +12.5, over four months. Outcome and axis match the agreed assessment. But the published e1 excerpt 'a statistically significant shift.' is cut from a method sentence: 'a confidence interval that excludes zero indicates a statistically significant shift.' Shortened, it reads as if the report found a significant shift, which those words don't say. Quote the opposition row or the full sentence instead.
